source.title: We Inspected Every Head In GPT-2 Small using SAEs So You Don’t Have To

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature analysis to GPT-2 Small and reports findings about feature interpretations and attention-head roles in a language model, rather than testing the original toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The study manually groups the top 10 SAE features attributed to each of GPT-2 Small's 144 attention heads and reports head-level findings. Results cited from prior posts are not recorded as this study's results. The text describes the H10.2 ablation outcome but does not provide its plotted values.
record.test_reason: The post uses attention-layer SAEs, trained and shown interpretable in earlier posts, as a tool to assign roles to GPT-2 Small's 144 heads. Its results are head-role annotations, head polysemanticity counts, and ablation and induction checks of those roles. It does not measure whether features are superposed or spread across neurons, nor whether SAEs recover a model's sparse features. Head-level polysemanticity is a related but different construct from V2–V4, which concern neurons and features.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE decoder-weight attribution is a useful tool for finding head roles, and that it recovers known heads (induction, previous token, successor, duplicate, copy suppression). They find that >90% of heads appear to do multiple tasks, with 14 plausibly monosemantic candidates, and caution that top-10 inspection cannot prove monosemanticity. They also report that features grow more abstract up to layer 9. Separately, H5.1 does long-prefix induction while H5.5 does standard induction, confirmed with non-SAE experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Uses attention-layer SAEs, decoder-weight attribution by head, and manual feature grouping, with selected ablation checks; it does not use the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Head-feature rankings may differ when using fraction of variance explained (FVE) rather than decoder-weight attribution; the authors recommend FVE for reproductions. Inspection is limited to the top 10 features per head.

fits_no_version.finding: Using top-10 decoder-weight-attributed SAE features, the authors judge >90% of GPT-2 Small attention heads to perform multiple tasks. Only 14/144 are plausibly monosemantic. H10.2's two inferred roles are confirmed by zero-ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention heads in LLMs are mostly polysemantic (attention-head-level polysemanticity/superposition).

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say dashboard-generation code is available by messaging one of the first two authors
record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The analysis is limited to the top 10 features per head and uses an imperfect attribution proxy. The authors describe their manual review as shallow and say it can produce false positives and false negatives. The H10.2 ablation results are described but numeric values are not present in the text.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep or geometry.
All: no capacity or importance analysis; polysemanticity is studied for heads, not neurons.
All: causes of polysemanticity are not examined.
Not tested here: SAE interpretability is taken from prior posts, and neuron-level spread is not measured.
All: completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested.
All: feature dimensionality is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is dropped. The post assumes SAE features are meaningful (shown in earlier posts) and uses them as a tool. Validation against known heads and ablations checks the technique, not superposition. Head polysemanticity concerns attention heads, not neurons, so it is placed in fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overlapping directions, and geometry.
Capacity competition, feature importance, and dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises from mechanisms other than capacity pressure; the study concerns attention heads, not neurons.
The study analyzes GPT-2 Small only; it does not measure feature distribution across all neurons or compare SAE recovery across models or dictionaries.
Feature completeness, stability, and canonical status are not tested.
The dimensionality or geometry of represented features is not tested.

rows.check: Measures attention-head polysemanticity (>90% of heads doing multiple tasks), inferred from top-10 SAE features. That concerns heads, not neurons, and not feature spread or SAE recovery, so it bears on no version. Recorded under fits_no_version.
